query: How do instrument specs and field stressors (humidity, dust, solar loading) justify QC drift thresholds (0.3°C, 1°C), and what explicit recalibration vs replacement actions and minimum data completeness should we set?

response.query: How do instrument specs and field stressors (humidity, dust, solar loading) justify QC drift thresholds (0.3°C, 1°C), and what explicit recalibration vs replacement actions and minimum data completeness should we set?
response.answer: QC drift thresholds justify recalibration or replacement when instrument specs show 0.3°C or 1°C deviation; recalibration every 6 months or replacement if data completeness falls below 95%.
